item.title: Deventer Travel Guide & History | Boiling Counterfeiters Alive
item.description:
Deventer, in the Netherlands, features medieval history around the Brink square and Lebuïnus Church, offering key things to see when you visit. Around 1809, soldiers in Napoleon's army shot holes into the execution kettle where a coin counterfeiter was once boiled alive.

item.title: Heerlen Travel Guide & History | From Coal Mines to Street Art
item.description:
Heerlen, in the Netherlands, is a place to visit for Roman and industrial history, featuring sights like Hoensbroek Castle, the Thermenmuseum, and the Glaspaleis. In 1965, the Dutch government announced the closure of the local coal mines, leading to a cultural transformation through street art and redevelopment.

item.title: Alkmaar Travel Guide & History | Secret Notes in Hollow Poles
item.description:
Alkmaar, in the Netherlands, features historic canals, the medieval Waaggebouw, and the Grote Sint Laurenskerk for tourists who visit to explore local history. In 1573, residents smuggled secret messages in hollow vaulting poles to request dike breaches, flooding surrounding lands to break a Spanish siege.

item.description:

item.title: Amsterdam Travel Guide & History | An Empire Built on Mud
item.description:
Amsterdam began as a muddy settlement behind a dam on the Amstel, and that history still shapes the things to see on a visit, from the canal rings to world-famous museums. In 1275, Count Floris V freed its residents from paying his tolls: a small privilege at the start of a long story.

item.title: Kampen Travel Guide & History | Why It Stopped Collecting Taxes
item.description:
Kampen, in the Netherlands, is a town made for wandering: the things to see on a visit include medieval city gates, church towers and a riverfront shaped by centuries of trade. In 1448 its citizens built a wooden bridge across the IJssel in just five months, and that's only the start of its Hanseatic history.
